reviewers.persona: Kursleiterin DaF (A1.1): Natürlichkeit, Niveau, Didaktik, Szenenplausibilität

method: Both reviewers read every German string again: title, start (7 Folge lines and the gist item), 3 inputs (30 lines) plus the flyer, 10 exam texts, 2 strategy cards, 8 redemittel, the 2 speaking parts with cards, openingLine, hintWords and 16 model turns, the writing task (situation, 3 Leitpunkte, checklist, model), 4 check lines, story beat and cliffhanger, every endLine and every explanation.de. We solved every item blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line only: 1 start gist, 15 input items, 12 structuredInput, 33 authored pool items, 12 reserve, 10 exam items, 8 check items and 4 proof items. For sentence_building we permuted the tiles and checked each V2 and V1 order against accepted[]. For generated items we traced what the player builds (src/components/course-v2/content.js dictationItems: answer = line.de, audio = line.say || line.de) and checked all 6 dictation sources for `say` (none has one now). Typed answers were graded the way the v2 player grades them: src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js (exact:number → checkNumber: digits must match, and an answer without digits is compared only with accepted forms that have none) on top of src/lib/lesson/check.js. Exam blocks were checked against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json (h1 6 × abc / 3 options / 2 plays / [32–53] words; h2 4 × R/F / 1 play / [29–47]; sp2 two topics, cards-ask; sp3 cards-request; s2 3 Leitpunkte, about 30 words) and against the rubrics sd1-sp2, sd1-sp3, sd1-s2, course-micro and course-micro-sp (all resolve). Word counts were recomputed with the validator's wordCount: h1 50/41/37/41/37/38, h2 31/31/33/30, flyer 47, model text 26, cliffhanger 25. We ran the validator's known-token machinery (knownForms + licensedForms at a1.1-u04) over every German string of the unit, not only inputs and exam texts, and looked up each unknown token's allocation in all eight lexicons. The grammar ceiling was checked against grammar-spine.json (g.akkusativ chunk a1.1-u04, productive a1.1-u06; g.kein a1.1-u06; g.pronomen-er-es-sie a1.1-u05; g.koennen with the Satzklammer a1.1-u08; g.zeitangaben-inversion a1.1-u07). The new-word load (32 entries, band [24–32]) was checked against level-profiles.json. The can-dos were read against registries/cando/a1.json, the cast against casts/series.json and casts/a1.json (ensemble-a1-1/-2 female, -3/-4 male; Arjun's WG), and the unit against curriculum/a1-1.md §4 and a1-1.json. We recomputed every price sum (market 2,20 + 3,60 + 0,90 + 1,80 + 0,50 = 9,00 ✓; total spend about 23,61 € of 50 € ✓). Every r1 and r2 finding was verified against the current file.

verdict: Not exit-ready, but the round-2 fixes are real, and one data line separates the unit from 0 BLOCKER / 0 MAJOR. All 37 earlier findings were verified: 33 are fixed or fixed-in-unit, one is expected (the LEX-02 ratchet), and 3 are still open (r1-F24 and r2-F11, one detector class for the rule-smith; r2-F09, the rule-cards owner). The German is correct on every model surface, and du/Sie is right everywhere. The LS4 texts no longer contradict the story, the dictations match their audio, and the exam blocks match sd1.json in items, options, plays and word bands. One MAJOR is new: ls2-i05 grades „neun“ as WRONG for a total the learner hears as „neun Euro“, while q04 in the same unit accepts „zehn“ as well as „10“. The 6 minors are one over the exit allowance. F02, F03, F04 and the h1-01 part of F05 are data edits in the unit. F06 is for the rule-cards owner and F07 for the rule-smith.

findings.quote: promptDe „Alles zusammen kostet ___ Euro.“ · accepted ["9", "9,00", "9.00"] · exact "number" · audio ls2-l10 say „… Das macht zusammen neun Euro. …“ — compare check.proofItems[3] (q04) accepted ["zehn", "10"]
findings.problem: The learner hears „neun Euro“, and the gap takes a word: „Alles zusammen kostet neun Euro.“ is correct German and exactly what was said. src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js grades exact:number items with checkNumber. An input without digits is compared only with accepted forms that contain no digits, and this item has none, so „neun“ is WRONG, not even TYPO, and no widget restricts the input to digits. The same unit accepts the number word in the same task shape (q04 „Arjun möchte ___ Eier.“ → „zehn“ or „10“), so the learner meets two conventions, and a correct listening answer is graded wrong.
findings.fix: Add „neun“ to accepted, with acceptedWhy „Zahl als Wort: so hört man es“. Alternatively, write the digit requirement into the prompt: „Schreiben Sie die Zahl: Alles zusammen kostet ___ Euro.“ (≤ 90 characters).
findings.proposedRule: ITM-07: a typed `exact: number` item whose key is a bare integer up to 100 must also accept its German number word, unless its promptDe asks for the digit („Schreiben Sie die Zahl“). Failing fixture: key „9“, accepted [„9“, „9,00“] and no „neun“. The test runs over all registered courses.

findings.path: explanation.de of steps[0].pool.items[6..8] (ls1-p07, -p08, -p09); steps[1].pool.items[8] (ls2-p09); steps[2].pool.items[4..7] (ls3-p05, -p06, -p07, -p08); steps[2].reserve[1] (ls3-r02); steps[2].structuredInput[0], [3] (ls3-s01, ls3-s04)
findings.quote: ls1-p08 tiles [sind / die Äpfel / billig / heute] → „die Äpfel ist Plural, deshalb sind.“ · ls3-p06 tiles [wir / zwei Kilo Kartoffeln / brauchen] → „Menge ohne Artikel: zwei Kilo Kartoffeln.“ · ls3-s01 „Nur zehn Eier ist Plural.“ · ls1-p05 „Das Verb ist steht auf Position 2.“ · ls3-s04 „Stück sagt man bei Sachen, die man zählt …“
findings.problem: In sentence_building the verb form is a tile the learner is given, so the only error possible is its position (V2 / V1 / verb-final). Nine explanations explain agreement instead, and ls3-p06 explains the Nullartikel, which the tiles already contain. A learner who builds „Die Äpfel heute billig sind“ is told about the plural, not about position 2, although these items carry the v2 purpose. The explanations also cite German forms without quotation marks, while their en twins quote them. In a unit that teaches ist/sind agreement, the feedback therefore displays apparent agreement errors („die Äpfel ist Plural“, „Nur zehn Eier ist Plural“, „Das Verb ist steht …“). ls3-s04 puts a relative clause („Sachen, die man zählt“) on an A1.1 feedback surface (level profile: subordinateClausesMax 0, feedback de-a1).
findings.fix: Lead with the order rule and quote the forms, e.g. ls1-p08 „„sind“ steht auf Position 2 („die Äpfel“ = Plural).“, ls3-p06 „„brauchen“ steht auf Position 2.“, ls3-s01 „„kosten“ = Plural: nur „zehn Eier“ passt.“, ls3-s04 „Stück: für Eier, Birnen, Brötchen. Nicht für Reis oder Milch.“
findings.proposedRule: ITM-11: when the verb of a sentence_building item is a tile, its explanation.de must name the position (the word „Position“, or errorTags contains v2-inv), and German forms cited in any explanation.de are quoted („…“). Failing fixture: ls1-p08 as it stands.

findings.quote: a1.1/lexicon.json: lx.kaese plural null, plural_kind "singular-only" · lx.milch plural null, plural_kind "singular-only"
findings.problem: Two of the four lemmas that the LS1 generator drills for article and plural have no plural. SCHEMA §3.2 does not define what lex.articlePlural builds for a singular-only lemma, and no rule stops such a source. With count 1, about every second run draws Käse or Milch, so the generated card either asks for a plural that does not exist (an item without a derivable key) or depends on player behaviour nobody has specified. The LS3 source (Ei, Tomate, Kartoffel, Flasche) shows the intended kind.
findings.fix: Change the source to ["lx.brot", "lx.apfel", "lx.banane", "lx.birne"]. All four have plural_kind regular and are u04 lemmas.
findings.proposedRule: ITM-06 (or REF-01): every source lemma of lex.articlePlural has plural_kind regular or plural-only, unless SCHEMA §3.2 defines an article-only card for singular-only lemmas. Failing fixture: a pool whose lex.articlePlural drills lx.milch.

findings.quote: cards learner „Essen und Trinken – Reis“, partner „Essen und Trinken – Milch“ · „Entschuldigung, wo ist der Reis?“ – „Der Reis ist dort.“ · „Wo ist die Milch?“ – „Die Milch ist hier.“
findings.problem: In Sprechen Teil 2 the candidates ask each other real questions on the topic word (research/01: „Einkaufen“, „Brot“ → „Wo kaufst du Brot?“). Round 2, which the r2-F08 fix added, is labelled „Essen und Trinken“, but its model is a shop-shelf role-play. Asking where the rice is fits neither the topic nor two candidates at an exam table, and „Der Reis ist dort“ points to nothing. The model therefore trains an off-topic question for the round whose topic the learner reads. The label words „Essen“ and „Trinken“ are also unglossed u09 lexis (lx.essen, lx.trinken a1.1-u09). Round 1 (Einkaufen: price, Gramm) is the same role-play but fits its topic, which is acceptable as an A1.1 scaffold.
findings.fix: Either (a) name the second topic after what it asks („Im Supermarkt“) in the cards, situationDe and openingLine, so the location questions (the „wo“ half of cd.a1.produkt-infos) fit their topic, or (b) keep „Essen und Trinken“ and model a real Teil-2 exchange that still asks where: „Wo kaufen Sie Reis?“ – „Im Supermarkt.“ / „Wo kaufen Sie Milch?“ – „Auf dem Markt.“ (all u04 words).

findings.path: content/course-v2/a1.1/rule-cards.json rc.artikel-genus-plural (shown in steps[0], steps[2]); rc.moechte (shown in steps[1])
findings.quote: rc.artikel-genus-plural „Unbestimmt heißt es ein (der, das) und eine (die).“ · table „unbestimmt | ein Apfel | ein Brot | eine Tomate“ (unchanged since r2) · rc.moechte „Mit einem zweiten Verb steht der Infinitiv am Ende: Ich möchte bezahlen.“
findings.problem: r2-F09 is still open. The card's rule holds only for the nominative and carries no case label, while this unit's frames are accusative (brauchen, möchte, kaufen) and its chunk is „Ich möchte einen Apfel“. A learner who applies the card writes ✗„Wir brauchen ein Käse / Ich möchte ein Apfel“, and u06 then has to unteach it (§9.5: a simplification that has become false in context). New in this round: rc.moechte previews the Satzklammer (möchte + Infinitiv), which the spine introduces with g.koennen at a1.1-u08, and uses bezahlen (a1.1-u09). No line, item or task in u04 uses möchte + Infinitiv, so the card states a rule the unit never practises, in a word the learner cannot yet read.
findings.fix: For the rule-cards owner. rc.artikel-genus-plural: label the row „unbestimmt (Nominativ)“ and add „Achtung: Ich möchte einen Apfel. (der → einen, Einheit 6)“. rc.moechte: drop the infinitive sentence at depth 1 (it belongs to u08/u09), or replace it with „Ich möchte ein Kilo Tomaten, bitte.“. Both cards stay within ruleCardMaxWords 60.

findings.path: GRM-04 advisories: start.folge.lines[0], [5]; steps[1].input.lines[7], [8]; steps[3].texts[1].lines[3], [4]; steps[4].task.modelTurns[3]
findings.quote: det.adjektiv-endung-unbestimmt on „bisschen“ · det.adjektiv-endung-nullartikel on „eine“ („für eine Wohnung“) and „möchten“ · det.trennbare-verben on „Was macht das zusammen?“ / „Das macht zusammen 7“ · det.imperativ-du-ihr [shape fallback] on „300“ / „200“ („300 Gramm, bitte.“)
findings.problem: All 7 advisories are false positives, and no construction goes beyond the ceiling. The detectors are unchanged since r1-F24 and r2-F11. The imperative shape fallback reads a sentence-initial numeral as a verb and will fire in every shopping, time and number unit. The Nullartikel detector fires on an indefinite article. Together they bury real advisories in noise.
findings.fix: No change to the unit. For the rule-smith: exclude digits and number words from the det.imperativ-du-ihr shape fallback, skip ein/eine/einen in det.adjektiv-endung-nullartikel, and add a stoplist for „bisschen“, the möchte paradigm and „macht (das) zusammen“.
findings.proposedRule: GRM-04 detector fixtures: „300 Gramm, bitte.“, „für eine Wohnung“, „ein bisschen Milch“, „Wir möchten Tomaten.“ and „Was macht das zusammen?“ must each produce no advisory. The test runs over all registered courses.

exitCheck.note: Exit needs 0 BLOCKER, 0 MAJOR, every criterion ≥ 4 and ≤ 5 logged MINOR. F01 is a one-string fix (add „neun“), and with F02 it lifts A to 4. F02 (explanations), F03 (generator source), F04 (Sp2 round 2) and the h1-01 and t9 parts of F05 are data edits inside the unit. After those edits the unit carries F05's lexicon-allocation residual (lexicon owner), F06 (rule-cards owner) and F07 (rule-smith): 3 logged minors. Class findings for the rule-smith: F01, F02, F03, F05 and F07, plus the still-open r1-F10 (TXT-02 double tolerance), r2-F01 (no rule reads `say`) and r2-F07 (LEX-01 skips the cliffhanger).
